points.t: Poorly defined, non-scaly, symptom-free pale macules merging on the back and trunk of a teenager or young adult, often with darker skin.
Probably Cutibacterium acnes in the follicles producing a depigmenting factor. Melanin is reduced but melanocyte numbers are normal.
Reassure. Options with variable evidence: benzoyl peroxide ± clindamycin, narrowband UVB, oral tetracycline.
Persistent, atypical, progressive patches in an adult may be hypopigmented mycosis fungoides. Refer.

points: Round or oval, **poorly bordered** pale macules that merge on the back and trunk, with or without the proximal limbs and neck.
**No scale.** This is the key difference from pityriasis versicolor.
**No preceding rash.** This is the key difference from post-inflammatory hypopigmentation.
More noticeable, and more often reported, in **darker skin**. Typically teens and young adults, possibly more common in women.
**Skin scrapings (KOH) are negative**, unlike pityriasis versicolor.
Dermoscopy shows ill-defined white macules with a faint pigment network. Biopsy is rarely needed.

cards.name: Pityriasis versicolor
cards.clue: **Fine scale**; ‘spaghetti and meatballs’ on KOH; often yellow-green under Wood’s lamp

cards.name: Post-inflammatory hypopigmentation
cards.clue: History of eczema, psoriasis or another rash at the same sites

cards.name: Vitiligo
cards.clue: Sharp, **chalk-white** patches, often on the hands, face and around orifices; bright white under Wood’s lamp

cards.name: Pityriasis alba
cards.clue: Faces of atopic children; mild scale

cards.name: Hypopigmented mycosis fungoides
cards.clue: Persistent, atypical, progressive patches in an adult. **Refer**

cards.name: Ash-leaf macules (tuberous sclerosis)
cards.clue: Congenital, leaf-shaped; look for other features of tuberous sclerosis

items.t: Atypical, persistent or progressive patches in an adult: exclude **hypopigmented mycosis fungoides**.
Congenital or ash-leaf-shaped macules with other signs: consider **tuberous sclerosis**.
‘Pityriasis versicolor’ that does not respond to antifungals: re-check for scale and do KOH.

pearls.t: Do not keep treating it as ‘fungus’. If there is scale, take a **KOH scraping first**.
Photoprotection still helps even out skin tone.
Manage expectations: response is **slow and often incomplete**.
